verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's source is public on GitHub, and community reports describe the license as BSD-3 (previously MIT). However, the current license adds custom branding clauses that commenters say move it away from permissive open source and make forking problematic, so 'open license' holds only with significant caveats. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license terms, evidence the license qualifies as OSI-approved open source without restrictive branding clauses.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: the most popular, most full-y featured OSS project
Open WebUI swapped MIT for BSD-3 five months before this change
